record.title: Brazil opens consultation on AI ethics guidance for human-subject research
record.summary: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s Ministry of Health opened a public consultation, scheduled through 31 March 2027, on three INAEP documents for ethical review of AI use in research with human participants: a guidance document, the MARIAH risk-assessment matrix, and a reference notebook. The Portuguese materials cover health and human/social-science research and recommend context-sensitive, proportionate review; MARIAH supports human committee deliberation and does not automatically approve or reject studies. The package is under consultation, not evidence of binding adoption or changed research practice.
organizations: Instância Nacional de Ética em Pesquisa (INAEP)

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Brazil’s Ministry of Health published an INAEP public consultation on 15 October 2026, open through 31 March 2027, covering the AI ethics guide, MARIAH risk matrix and reference notebook for human-subject research.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The consulted guide addresses research in health and human/social sciences and frames review around use context and proportionality; MARIAH is described as a support instrument for risk identification and documentation, not an automatic approval/rejection system.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: INAEP presents the package as a way to improve ethical assessment of AI use in human-subject research, including participant protection, risk identification and mitigation, transparency, data quality and human oversight.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The public page identifies the package as a consultation and the documents as guidance and assessment tools; this record does not establish binding adoption or implementation.

evidence_gaps.description: The final text and institutional status after the consultation are unknown.
No evidence shows whether Brazilian CEPs adopt MARIAH or how it changes protocol review, safeguards, workload or research practice.

brief.importance_rationale: If finalized and used by Brazilian research ethics committees, the package could change how AI use, participant and community risks, data governance, and proportionate safeguards are documented across health and human/social-science research. Its national scope makes the direction meaningful, while consultation status and unknown uptake cap the present consequence.
limitations: The documents are under public consultation and may change.
The consultation page and documents do not establish final adoption, legal force, committee uptake, or effects on research practice.
No submissions, consultation outcome analysis, or implementation evidence were reviewed.
organizations: Instância Nacional de Ética em Pesquisa (INAEP)
brief.summary: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s Ministry of Health opened a public consultation, scheduled through 31 March 2027, on three INAEP documents for ethical review of AI use in research with human participants: a guidance document, the MARIAH risk-assessment matrix, and a reference notebook. The Portuguese materials cover health and human/social-science research and recommend context-sensitive, proportionate review; MARIAH supports human committee deliberation and does not automatically approve or reject studies. The package is under consultation, not evidence of binding adoption or changed research practice.

technical.claimed_result: INAEP says the consultation aims to improve practical ethical guidance and instruments for researchers, institutions and CEPs.
technical.demonstrated_result: Official Portuguese materials and the three linked documents exist; they outline contextual, proportional review and human committee deliberation. The consultation itself does not establish adoption or effects.
technical.implementation_status: Public consultation open; final post-consultation text, binding status, institutional uptake and implementation are unknown.
technical.mechanism: The three-document package separates evaluative guidance, a structured risk matrix (MARIAH), and supporting ethical/conceptual/legal/methodological rationale. It asks protocols to describe the AI’s function, data and affected people, decision influence, validation, oversight and lifecycle risks so committees can document a proportional human judgment.
technical.novelty: The package publicly joins general ethics guidance, a dedicated AI-risk matrix and reference rationale for human-subject research across health and human/social-science fields in Brazil.
technical.regime: Brazilian research involving human participants in health, human/social sciences, and interdisciplinary protocols; the package is under public consultation from 15 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
technical.reproducibility: Primary documents were directly opened and read in Portuguese. No survey of committee use or policy implementation was conducted.
technical.strongest_baseline: The source documents establish a newly consulted national guidance package. No prior national instrument comparison or resulting practice baseline was evaluated in this activation.

brief.title: Brazil opens consultation on AI ethics guidance for human-subject research
brief.why_it_matters: The package would give Brazilian researchers and ethics committees a shared structure for describing AI’s role, data and affected populations, model validation, human oversight and lifecycle risks in human-subject protocols. If finalized and applied, it could influence AI research governance across a large health and social-science system. Current documents establish proposed guidance and consultation only; they do not show adoption, committee uptake or effects.
